context_requirements: Expression of ENTPD3 (CD39L3) in the assayed cell line
Functional extracellular nucleotide (ATP/ADP) signaling tone that can be modulated by NTPDase activity
Presence of purinergic receptors (e.g., P2Y1) whose activation state depends on extracellular nucleotide levels
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Consistent induction of immediate-early or purinergic-signaling target genes across multiple lines
Evidence of ENTPD3 expression and measurable extracellular ATP/ADP hydrolysis in these lines coupled with transcriptional responses

evidence.supports: E-NTPDase inhibitor ARL67156 increased proliferation of rat retinal progenitors, showing NTPDase inhibition can modulate cell behavior via extracellular adenine nucleotide/P2Y1 signaling
CD39/NTPDase regulates extracellular ATP-mediated innate immune responses, indicating NTPDase activity can influence transcriptional programs in immune contexts
